key_insight: Adjusting ultrasound-driven airflow can remotely switch a heated object's surface between suppressed natural convection for heat retention and enhanced convection for cooling.
engineering_relevance: Target-selective, noncontact convection control could enable localized temperature management for food, beverages, manufacturing, and laboratory processes.
method: Direct an ultrasonic beam at a heat-source surface to generate acoustic streaming.
Adjust ultrasonic output intensity to accelerate or decelerate near-surface airflow.
Switch between heat-retaining and cooling conditions without contacting the object.
evidence_signal: Experiments demonstrated intensity-dependent switching between heat retention and cooling, though the abstract reports no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Practical operating ranges, energy efficiency, and robustness to ambient airflow remain unspecified in the abstract.
paper_title: Remote and Noncontact Acceleration and Suppression of Heat Convection on Object Surfaces using Intensity-Adjusted Acoustic Streaming
